generic_name: Immune Globulin G (IgG) with Hippurate and Maltose
purpose: This medicine helps boost your immune system when your body does not make enough antibodies on its own. It is used to help prevent serious infections in people with weakened immune systems. Doctors also use it to treat certain immune-related conditions like immune thrombocytopenia (low platelets) or Kawasaki disease.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally makes proteins called antibodies to fight off germs and infections. This medicine is made from donated human plasma and contains ready-made antibodies that your body can use right away. Think of it like borrowing a supply of soldiers to help your body fight off harmful bacteria and viruses until your own immune system can catch up.
common_side_effects: Headache, mild fever, chills, nausea, tiredness, muscle aches, and flushing or redness at the injection site are common. Some people may feel a little flu-like for a day or two after the infusion. Slowing down the infusion rate often helps reduce these effects.
warnings: Rarely, this medicine can cause serious kidney problems, blood clots, or a severe allergic reaction. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, swelling, or severe headache. People with certain blood types or kidney problems may need extra monitoring. Do not use if you have a history of severe allergic reactions to human immunoglobulin products.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated based on your body weight and the condition being treated. It is given as a slow drip into a vein (IV infusion), usually every 3 to 4 weeks. Your doctor and nurse will monitor you closely during each infusion and may adjust the dose based on how you respond.
